# Glossary {#sec-app-d}

6LoWPAN
: IPv6 over Low-Power Wireless Personal Area Networks; an adaptation layer that compresses and fragments IPv6 packets for small radio frames (@sec-ch11).

ACK / NACK
: Acknowledgment / negative acknowledgment, confirming whether data was received.

Actuator
: A device that converts a control signal into a physical effect such as motion, light or sound (@sec-ch07).

ADC
: Analog-to-digital converter; measures a voltage and converts it to a number (@sec-ch03).

AEAD
: Authenticated encryption with associated data; encryption that also guarantees integrity, such as AES-GCM (@sec-ch14).

BLE
: Bluetooth Low Energy (@sec-ch10).

Border router
: A router connecting a low-power network such as 6LoWPAN or Thread to the wider IP network (@sec-ch11).

Broker
: In publish/subscribe systems such as MQTT, the server that receives messages and forwards them to subscribers (@sec-ch12).

Certificate (X.509)
: A signed statement binding a public key to an identity (@sec-ch15).

CoAP
: Constrained Application Protocol; a REST protocol over UDP for constrained devices (@sec-ch12).

Constrained device
: A device with limited memory, processing and energy (@sec-ch09).

Debouncing
: Filtering the rapid on/off transitions of a mechanical switch (@sec-ch03).

Deep sleep
: An ESP32 low-power mode in which only the RTC domain stays powered (@sec-ch10).

DODAG
: Destination-oriented directed acyclic graph; the routing structure built by RPL (@sec-ch11).

Duty cycle
: The fraction of time a signal is on (PWM), or that a device or radio is active.

eFuse
: One-time-programmable memory bits inside a chip, used for keys and security configuration (@sec-ch16).

Edge / fog computing
: Processing close to where data is produced, between devices and the cloud (@sec-ch18).

Encapsulation
: Wrapping data with each protocol layer's header as it moves down the stack (@sec-ch08).

Fail-safe state
: The state that causes the least harm when something fails (@sec-ch07).

Flash encryption
: Transparent encryption of a device's external flash memory (@sec-ch16).

GATT
: Generic Attribute Profile; the BLE data model of services and characteristics (@sec-ch10).

GPIO
: General-purpose input/output pin.

HMAC
: Hash-based message authentication code; proves integrity and authenticity with a shared key (@sec-ch14).

Hysteresis
: Using separate on and off thresholds to prevent rapid switching near a set point (@sec-ch07).

I²C
: Inter-Integrated Circuit; a two-wire, addressed serial bus (@sec-ch05).

IMU
: Inertial measurement unit; an accelerometer and gyroscope, sometimes with a magnetometer (@sec-ch06).

Interrupt / ISR
: A hardware signal that pauses normal execution to run an interrupt service routine (@sec-ch03).

Interoperability
: The ability of systems to exchange information and use it (@sec-ch13).

LLN
: Low-power and lossy network (@sec-ch11).

LoRa / LoRaWAN
: A long-range, low-power radio modulation, and the network protocol built on it (@sec-ch10).

LPWAN
: Low-power wide-area network.

Matter
: A smart-home interoperability standard running over IP on Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Thread (@sec-ch13).

MEMS
: Micro-electro-mechanical systems; microscopic mechanical structures in silicon, used in most motion and pressure sensors.

MQTT
: A lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol (@sec-ch12).

mTLS
: Mutual TLS, in which both client and server present certificates (@sec-ch15).

NAT
: Network address translation, which maps private addresses to a public one (@sec-ch08).

ODA loop
: Observe–Decide–Act, the cycle connecting sensing to actuation (@sec-ch07).

OTA update
: Over-the-air update: delivering new firmware through the network (@sec-ch16).

PKI
: Public-key infrastructure; the certificate authorities, certificates and policies that establish trust (@sec-ch15).

Provisioning
: Giving a device its identity, credentials and configuration (@sec-ch15).

Pull-up / pull-down resistor
: A resistor that holds an input at a defined level when nothing else drives it (@sec-ch03).

PWM
: Pulse-width modulation; switching a signal rapidly to control average power or encode a value (@sec-ch03).

QoS
: Quality of service; in MQTT, the delivery guarantee level (@sec-ch12).

Real-time system
: A system that must respond within a specified time (@sec-ch04).

Replay attack
: Resending a captured valid message to repeat its effect (@sec-ch14).

RPL
: IPv6 Routing Protocol for Low-Power and Lossy Networks (@sec-ch11).

RSSI / SNR
: Received signal strength indicator / signal-to-noise ratio.

RTOS
: Real-time operating system (@sec-ch04).

SBOM
: Software bill of materials; a list of all software components in a product (@sec-ch16).

Secure boot
: Verifying the signature of each piece of software before running it (@sec-ch16).

Secure element
: A tamper-resistant chip that stores keys and performs cryptography without exposing keys (@sec-ch15).

SoC
: System on a chip; a microcontroller or processor integrated with larger subsystems such as radios.

SPI
: Serial Peripheral Interface; a fast synchronous bus with a chip-select line per device (@sec-ch05).

STRIDE
: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege; a threat-modeling mnemonic (@sec-ch14).

Thing Description
: A W3C JSON-LD document describing a device's properties, actions and events (@sec-ch13).

Thread
: An IPv6 mesh networking protocol on 802.15.4 radios (@sec-ch11).

TinyML
: Machine learning on microcontrollers (@sec-ch18).

TLS / DTLS
: Transport Layer Security, and its datagram (UDP) variant.

TSN
: Time-Sensitive Networking; IEEE standards for deterministic Ethernet (@sec-ch10).

UART
: Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter; point-to-point serial communication without a clock wire (@sec-ch05).

Vertical slice
: A thin, end-to-end working version of a whole system (@sec-ch20).

Watchdog timer
: A timer that resets the processor unless software services it regularly (@sec-ch04).
